items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And that was Lionel Hampton. That's the boy I remember walking around Chicago.

ctx.x: Wait a minute. Okay, it's going now. Can you tell about when you joined Louis?

When I joined Louis, yeah. Louis came back. He was on his way to California to play at Sebastons. Which later became famous and one of the Chicago musicians became famous. And that was Lionel Hampton. That's the boy I remember walking around Chicago.
Okay, it's going if you want to state your name.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: We had, as I said, Lionel Hampton carried his drum all the time up on his arms. And Bernie Young, and about four or five others.

ctx.x: You never had another job then. Huh? You never had a dead job until later.

Well, at that time I didn't have to work. I had a great mother, you understand. And my mother was a pretty good business woman, and my father was a brick mason, although, he wasn't allowed, they wouldn't give him a card in Chicago, so he started to, he was a foreman at the IC Roundhouse. See, now, doing this blue blood plague around here, all out the Annunciation Street, he laid bricks all out there, you understand, and they had to put in these concrete instead of the top of the floors and the groves and things…

We had a mouthpiece over here and a cigarette in here. I looked at this guy and said, I wanted to get this guy to play with this cigarette in his mouth on one side and play on the side. And so we had a little march. So finally Grand Marshal came back saying, fellas, when I whistle, I mean for the drum to start plop, plop, plop, plop, plop, plop, plop, and finally in the bass room, jing, with the cymbals, see. And so this little tune, it went like this. I never will forget this. Ta-da-da-da-da-da-da.…
